Data for Humanity · Transport safety · TfL 2025

How safe is cycling
in London?

TfL estimates 2.19 killed or seriously injured cyclists per million cycle journey stages in 2025. That rate is below its 2010–14 baseline, but rose from 2024. Explore the collision records—and what the rate does and does not prove.

What this tells us

Collision records point to places to investigate, not a verdict on safety.

TfL’s exposure-adjusted KSI rate fell 17.4% from its 2010–14 baseline, then rose 6.9% in 2025. Separately, Westminster has the most raw casualty records (465). Borough counts are not risk rates, and neither trend establishes that infrastructure caused or prevented an injury.

Data, method & limitations

Counts: TfL’s 2025 casualty extract is filtered to Casualty Mode of Travel = Pedal Cycle and joined to its attendant extract by _Collision Id. The result contains 5,675 cyclist casualties in 5,614 collisions: 6 fatal, 1,196 serious and 4,473 slight. The injury-risk annex separately publishes rates per million cycle journey stages; rates are shown directly from that annex.

Limits: TfL injury collision data excludes near misses and damage-only incidents. Borough counts are not adjusted for cycling volume. The Cycling Infrastructure Database catalogued by London Datastore is a 2017–18 snapshot, not a 2025 inventory; this analysis cannot establish infrastructure effects.

Map: The source uses British National Grid. Display coordinates are approximate; counts and filters use TfL borough labels. A collision can injure several cyclists.
